title: Ops Wrangler: atomic admin-utility registry and runbook task composer
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build an 'Ops Wrangler' microservice and console surface that lets SREs and oncall engineers register small, idempotent admin utilities (scripts, kubectl wrappers, api calls) as first-class tasks and compose them into runbook steps. The goal is to reduce blast radius of ad-hoc shell fixes, improve reproducibility, and enable automated safe replay for frequent support flows. The system should include: a typed task manifest, parameter schema and validation, RBAC scoping per team, dry-run sandboxing, telemetry hooks (cost, latency, success/failure classified), and automatic audit trail entries that feed the Console. It must interoperate with our existing runbook runner and Ops Playflow APIs without requiring teams to rewrite their playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Registry API to create/read/update tasks with versioned manifests and parameter schemas (OpenAPI/JSON Schema) and per-task RBAC metadata
Console tab to list registered utilities with search, team filter, and a safe ‘try in sandbox’ button wired to a namespaced dry-run environment
Runbook composer that can insert registry tasks as steps and export a taskified runbook that the runner can execute atomically
Telemetry emitted for each task execution: start/end timestamps, duration, token usage estimate (if applicable), exit code and structured outcome label (success/soft-fail/human-intervention)
All executions produce immutable audit records (user, task version, params, dry-run flag) persisted to our audit store and visible in the Console trace

Security review completed and safety gates enforced: mandatory user confirmation for destructive tasks, allowlist for sensitive parameter types, and integration with team KMS for any secrets used by utilities
comments: 2025-01-22 Sofia Patel: scoped proposal and problem statement after two post-incident retros. Noted recurring fixes for cache poisoning and evict-and-warm sequences; these are primary early targets.
